description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
3 blocks without inner LN: attention sums signed residues for all 65 primes <=316, ReLU bumps at multiples flag divisibility, priority gate picks smallest, per-digit mux plus copy head for primes.
relu_comb_v1 with rectangular attention maps, per-block MLP widths, no attention in block 2 and only 10 position dims: same circuit, sized to what it uses.
Block 2 writes the winning prime straight into 30 one-hot digit registers plus an ANY-factor bit, instead of keeping 65 first-factor dims.
Digit registers with unsigned digit residues in [0,p): measures how many extra bumps dropping the signed trick costs.
Ablation: trial-divide only by the 25 primes up to 97; composites with a larger smallest factor fall through to the copy head and are wrong.

Numeric circuit: one attention head reads n as a place-value weighted mean, one periodic pulse neuron per prime detects divisibility, priority gate writes the prime's digits, 4 gates select the answer digit, tangent-line head decodes it.
pulse_placevalue_v1 in float32: tests whether n/p and the cos pulse keep enough precision without doubles.
Pulse sharpness just below the theoretical limit 1/(1-cos(2pi/313)) = 4962: near misses for p=313 should start firing.
Two blocks: a two-hidden-layer sieve MLP (pulse neurons then priority gates) replaces the 65 flag dims of the state vector.
The 65x65 priority matrix becomes a parameter-free lateral inhibition: each pulse is suppressed by the running sum of all pulses from smaller primes.
Drops the ANY dim: a nonzero digit of the winning prime closes the copy gate by itself.
Replaces the 10 position one-hots with a place-value score, s, s^2 and 3 step flags; the copy head becomes Gaussian attention -BETA(i-(s-5))^2 in a 2-dim head.
Ablation of the compact sieve: only the 6 primes up to 13.
Ablation of the compact sieve: drops only p=313, the largest prime the task can need.
Pulse sharpness 1000, far below the 4962 needed to silence near misses for p=313: large primes leak about 0.8 at n = kp +- 1.
Restores the standard final LayerNorm: the tangent-line head reads A and ONE relative to an always-zero dim, which cancels LayerNorm's mean shift.
Restores the standard pre-LN blocks: a huge constant anchor dim fixes LayerNorm's scale, and all weights read relative to an always-zero dim to cancel its mean shift.
Pre-LN blocks with the anchor lowered to 1e9, balancing rounding noise (grows with the anchor) against LayerNorm scale drift (shrinks with it).
Pre-LN blocks with a mirror dim holding -n: the state sum no longer depends on n, removing the first-order LayerNorm scale drift.

ReLU only, 2 blocks, no periodic neuron: 5 Gaussian-attention heads read one-hot digits, a two-hidden-layer MLP does the residue comb and cumsum inhibition, numeric gates and tangent-line head as in the sieve.
relu_compact in float32: all residue signals are small integers, so unlike the pulse model it should not need doubles.
Replaces each 3-ReLU bump with one triangular unit relu(1-|u|), so the comb needs 195 hidden units instead of 585.
Softer attention, BETA 5: neighbouring positions get weight e^-5, so each residue sum is off by a small fraction of an integer.
BETA 10: the leak e^-10 times the largest residue 150 is about 0.007, predicted to be safe where BETA 5 is not.
BETA 10 with a narrow bump relu(1-2|u|): near misses at y = c +- 1 now sit in a dead zone, so attention leaks produce exactly zero flags.
Narrow bump at BETA 15, to look for the smallest attention sharpness that keeps every n correct.
Heads read digits as numbers: y_p = sum of d_i * (10^i mod p). A far smaller state, but the range of y_p grows ninefold and needs many more bumps.
Factors the comb: one shared residue sum y_p per prime, one hand-set tooth offset per bump, and a fixed sum of the bumps of each prime, removing the 536x65 bump-to-flag matrix.
Each prime uses the multiplier c that makes the five weights c*10^i mod p smallest; p divides n iff it divides c*n, and a smaller y_p range needs fewer teeth.
Removes the copy head: block 1 already stored the 5 digits, so 5 step-gated units replace block 2's attention, leaving one attention layer in the model.
Ablation: no lateral inhibition, so numbers with several prime factors write the digits of all of them at once.
tri_one_attention in half precision: y_p stays in the low hundreds, so even 16-bit floats may represent every signal exactly.
Float16 with BETA 8 and a finite '=' weight of -1000: the best-multiplier coefficients are small, so softer attention may stay inside the bump's dead zone.
Float16 with BETA 12, between the failing BETA 8 and the passing BETA 15.
Ablation: factor digits no longer close the copy path, so a composite's prompt digits add onto its factor digits.
Ablation of the final architecture: only the 15 primes up to 47.
Ablation of the final architecture: only the 46 primes up to 199.
Full prime list at BETA 15 in float16 with the standard final LayerNorm restored, read relative to an always-zero dim.

Recommended model: one attention layer reads the digits, a residue comb with best multipliers and narrow bumps finds divisors, cumsum inhibition picks the smallest, 8 step gates and a tangent-line head emit the answer. Float16, no LayerNorm, BETA 15.
tri_final at BETA 10, to narrow the sharpness threshold between the failing BETA 8 and the passing BETA 12.
